operations.evidence: The bulletin reports investigative outcomes assigned to notifiable offences recorded in England and Wales between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026.
The reporting period is national and does not identify parcel-level conditions.
The fraud and Computer Misuse Act outcomes chapter was excluded while City of London Police aligned legacy Action Fraud data with Report Fraud.
Missing fraud outcome data must not be imputed from other crime categories.
Firearm and knife or sharp instrument offences are subsets of other offence categories rather than separate offence categories.
Subset figures must not be added to broad offence totals as if mutually exclusive.
Victim-based offences include violence against the person, sexual offences, theft, robbery, and criminal damage and arson.
This grouping is analytical and does not establish local exposure for a specific property.
Non-victim-based offences include public disorder, drug offences, possession of weapons, handling stolen goods, and other offences against the state.
Police activity and enforcement priorities can strongly affect these recorded volumes.
The robbery charge or summons rate increased from 7.5% to 10.5% compared with the previous year.
The rate reflects case outcomes and investigation maturity, not neighbourhood safety.
The theft charge or summons rate increased from 7.3% to 9.1% compared with the previous year.
The rate cannot be interpreted as the probability of detection for a specific incident.
Evidential-difficulty outcomes accounted for 47.6% of sexual offences.
Outcome categories describe investigation closure and do not measure offence prevalence.
Evidential-difficulty outcomes accounted for 51.7% of rape offences.
The figure is national and subject to later outcome revisions.
Evidential-difficulty outcomes accounted for 39.0% of all victim-based offences.
Broad outcome shares should not be transferred to local parcels.
Rape offences assigned a charge or summons outcome took an average of 438 days to investigate.
Long investigation duration means year-end charge rates are incomplete and can rise later.
Violence against the person offences assigned a charge or summons outcome took an average of 55 days.
Median or average processing time is not a measure of crime severity.
Theft offences assigned a charge or summons outcome took an average of 27 days.
Outcome timing cannot identify risk at a specific location.
No suspect was identified in 40.9% of victim-based cases closed in this way.
Closure reason percentages are influenced by offence mix and evidence availability.
No suspect was identified in 69.4% of theft cases closed in this way.
This national theft outcome share is not a parcel-level clearance probability.
Evidential difficulties accounted for 35.6% of non-victim-based outcomes.
The category aggregates different offence types and investigative circumstances.
No suspect was identified in 22.8% of non-victim-based outcomes.
Some non-victim offences are police-generated, so direct comparison with victim-based offences is inappropriate.
Out-of-court disposals accounted for 12.1% of non-victim-based outcomes.
Disposal shares reflect eligibility and policing practice, not underlying local crime levels.
At year-end, 9.5% of non-victim-based offences remained under investigation.
Open investigations can later receive revised outcomes.
The median time from recording to assigned outcome for non-victim-based offences was 17 days.
A national median hides force and offence-level variation.
All 40 wave51 Home Office source IDs are unique and use a new indexed prefix.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
